title: Supreme Court: Letters Patent Bench Can't Overturn a Reasonable Writ Court Order, Reinstates Dismissed Registrar
case_name: R. Saravanan v. Periyar University, represented by its Registrar & Ors.
card_summary: A single judge had set aside the removal of Periyar University's Deputy Registrar, finding the disciplinary findings against him unsupported by evidence, but a Division Bench reversed that on the University's appeal. The Supreme Court restored the single judge's order, holding a Letters Patent Bench cannot interfere with an otherwise just writ court decision merely because it takes a different view.
card_tip: An intra-court appeal bench needs a glaring, demonstrable error to reverse a writ court, not just a different reading of the same record; frame Letters Patent appeals accordingly.
verification_notes: Decision date, bench (Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar) and citation 2026 INSC 1136 cross-checked across ETV Bharat, Verdictum and Courtbook reports, all dated 19-20 October 2026 reporting a 16 October 2026 judgment.
